paper_title: Thermal-Cycling-aware Dynamic Reliability Management in Many-Core System-on-Chip

scenario.figure_or_table: Figure 2 and Figure 3; Motivating Example and Experimental Setup Section V
scenario.description: 8×8 many-core NoC-based system executing multi-threaded PARSEC benchmarks with applications entering and leaving the system at runtime. Thermal cycling awareness evaluated across mapping, scheduling, and DPM units. System uses per-core temperature sensors and Coffin-Mason thermal cycling reliability model.
scenario.architecture: 8×8 mesh-based NoC many-core, Niagara2 cores, squared floorplan, 109mm² chip area, 16nm technology, private L1 cache per core, distributed shared L2 cache, four memory controllers, global controller with feedback loop for mapping, scheduling, and DPM. Per-core temperature sensors, per-system power sensor, DVFS and PCPG tunable per core.
scenario.workload: Multi-threaded PARSEC benchmark suite, randomly selected applications entering system at runtime, 25 application executions for main simulation. Memory-intensive and compute-intensive application types characterized for memory affinity profiling.
scenario.operating_point: Thermal Design Power (TDP) of 90W. Steady-state condition: δT = 20°C, TMax = 70°C, ∆T = 1 hour, m = 10 cycles, baseline MTTFTC = 10 years. Control periods: long-term 1–2 hours (mapping), short-term milliseconds (scheduling), DPM feedback loop with PID controller. Temperature sampling period approximately 1 second.

original_setup.solver: Noculator NOC-based many-core simulator based on Intel PIN binary instrumentation
original_setup.optimizer: MOC multi-objective power management with PID controller extended with thermal cycling metric (avgAmplitude × maxT)
original_setup.controller: Global controller with Reliability Analysis unit, Reliability-aware Mapping unit, Reliability-aware Thread Scheduling unit, and Reliability-aware DPM unit; rainflow counting algorithm for thermal cycle extraction; low-pass filter for temperature trace processing
original_setup.benchmark: Multi-threaded PARSEC benchmark suite; 25 application executions randomly selected from repository; applications enter and leave system at runtime

thermal_observable.location: per-core MTTF computed across 8×8 many-core system
thermal_observable.aggregation: minimum MTTF, average MTTF, and standard deviation of core MTTF values reported in Fig. 5 and Fig. 6

physical_mismatches.reason: Simulator-based evaluation using Noculator with synthetic PARSEC workloads rather than silicon measurements; no experimental validation on actual hardware

Thermal cycling reliability model parameters (EaTC, b, Tth, k, ATC) empirically fitted to achieve MTTFTC = 10 years under assumed steady-state conditions (δT=20°C, TMax=70°C, ∆T=1 hour, m=10); no independent validation of Coffin-Mason equation accuracy for this technology node
Per-core temperature sensors modeled in simulation via Hotspot thermal model; actual sensor accuracy, resolution, and sampling jitter not characterized
DVFS and PCPG tuning actuators implemented in simulation without accounting for transition delays, energy costs, or voltage regulator dynamics
Global controller architecture assumes centralized decision making with feedback; scalability and communication latency for large many-core systems not addressed

studio_assumptions: architectural configuration assumes 8×8 mesh-based NoC with Niagara2 cores, 109mm² chip area in 16nm technology, and 90W TDP from McPAT and Lumos; floorplan is squared without specification of core placement details or thermal via distribution

Workload composition: multi-threaded PARSEC applications randomly selected and issued at runtime; application mix, arrival rates, thread counts, and execution durations are not fully specified; only 25 application executions simulated

Thermal model: Hotspot steady-state thermal simulator integrated; assumes homogeneous silicon properties, uniform heat spreader, and no transient thermal effects beyond the 1-second temperature sampling window

Reliability model: Coffin-Mason equation (Eq. 1) with fixed parameters (EaTC=0.42eV, b=2.35, Tth=1°C, k=8.62×10⁻⁵eV/K, ATC fitted); rainflow counting and Miner's rule applied to extract and aggregate thermal cycles from low-pass filtered temperature traces

Control periods: long-term mapping decisions over 1–2 hours; short-term scheduling over milliseconds; DPM PID controller sampling at power sensor frequency; no interaction or timing conflicts between controllers specified

Performance target: nominal baseline scheduling and mapping from [5], [8], [14] without reliability enhancement; proposed approach compared against MOC [14] and reliability-aware mapping from [2]; no explicit performance constraints or SLA targets stated
Power constraint: TDP of 90W enforced by MOC DPM unit; no per-core power limits or dark silicon models specified beyond TDP
Memory system: four memory controllers, distributed L2 cache, per-core private L1; memory contention and interference not explicitly modeled in reliability decisions
Baseline profiling: memory affinity metrics (hits and misses) pre-profiled at design time per application type; no dynamic profiling or online adaptation of affinity models
missing_inputs: Complete PARSEC benchmark trace files or execution profiles used for workload generation; reproduction requires access to identical random application selection sequence
Exact floorplan coordinates and thermal via layout for the 8×8 many-core; only squared floorplan and 109mm² area specified
Detailed Hotspot thermal model configuration file (layer stack, material properties, die thickness, package parameters, ambient temperature)
McPAT and Lumos model configurations for power and physical scaling parameters in 16nm technology; source files or configuration dumps not provided
Complete algorithm pseudo-code and implementation details for the low-pass filter (cutoff frequency, filter order) and rainflow counting algorithm parameters
Detailed mapping and scheduling policy decision logs from the 25-application simulation run; only aggregate statistics (MIN, STD, AVG MTTF) in Fig. 5 and Fig. 6 reported
Per-core temperature traces and thermal cycle extraction results (peak, valley, amplitude, frequency) for baseline and proposed approach; needed to validate rainflow algorithm correctness
Validation of MTTFTC = 10 years steady-state assumption; independent measurement or cross-reference to Coffin-Mason parameters from silicon characterization data not provided
Source code or detailed implementation of Noculator simulator modifications for thermal cycling metrics and reliability-aware units; only algorithmic descriptions (Algorithms 1–3) provided
Specification of ready queue scheduling discipline (FIFO, priority), thread context switch overhead, and scheduling epoch duration for the reliability-aware scheduler
